title: SDKs: unified iterator abstractions and retry profiles for embeddings + rerank
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce a small, idiomatic iterator/stream helper and a set of retry profiles across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to provide consistent pagination, batching, backoff, and streaming ergonomics for embeddings and reranking endpoints.
background: Multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc helpers for embeddings pagination and reranking batching. Inconsistencies across language SDKs cause confusion for product engineers and increase support load. We also lack a unified set of retry/backoff profiles tuned to common infra failure modes (rate limits, transient 5xx, socket resets).
proposal: Deliver a cross-SDK pattern: 1) a lightweight iterator abstraction that exposes both pull (next) and async streaming semantics (where supported) for embeddings and rerank results; 2) standardized batching helpers (batch_by_tokens, batch_by_items) with deterministic ordering; 3) three retry profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) with clear defaults per endpoint; 4) example cookbooks for common usage (bulk-embed, rerank-streaming-realtime). Implement in Python, TypeScript, and Go with matching API surface and docs.
tradeoffs: Keeping the iterator surface minimal favors ergonomics but restricts advanced use-cases (custom sharding/parallelism) — recommend exposing lower-level primitives for power users. Choosing safe defaults for retries reduces support noise but may mask upstream capacity problems; include observability hooks so customers can tweak profiles. Implementing streaming parity in Go will require additional goroutine coordination vs. Node/Python async streams.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed — prototypes in Python/TS show parity on next()/stream() behavior. Found mismatch in how Go SDK handled partial failures during batch mapping.
2026-02-27: Review session with SDK leads — agreed on function names: iterator(), stream(), batch_by_tokens(), retry_profile(name).
2026-03-03: PR #842 in typescript-sdk opened with iterator + batch helpers; included e2e example for embeddings pagination. https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/842
2026-03-07: Python implementation initial PR #170 submitted; CI failing on edge-case where chunking interacts with streaming backpressure. https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/170
2026-03-10: Go design note posted — decided to expose channel-based streams and a convenience Iterator wrapper. Blocking on review from Go maintainer due to concurrency semantics.
acceptance_criteria: API parity: Python, TypeScript, and Go expose iterator() and stream() helpers with documented behavior
Batch helpers: batch_by_tokens and batch_by_items available in all SDKs and tested with large inputs
Retry profiles: fast, balanced, conservative implemented and selectable; default profile is balanced for embeddings and rerank
Examples: one cookbook per language showing bulk-embed with pagination and rerank streaming use-case
Integration tests: end-to-end tests against staging endpoints validating ordering and no-dup semantics
Docs: Console/SDK docs updated with migration notes and recommended profiles
qa_notes: Focus on ordering guarantees when batching + retrying. Test with simulated 429s and mid-response socket resets to ensure idempotency or safe retries. Verify that streaming consumers receive partial results promptly and that backpressure doesn't drop items.
